```{r setup}
library(arrow); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr)
library(stringr); library(scales); library(gt); library(here)
options(arrow.skip_nul = TRUE)

ANALYSIS <- here("phase2", "data", "analysis", "deliverable06")
OUTPUT   <- here("phase2", "output", "deliverable06")
FIGS     <- file.path(OUTPUT, "figures")

verdicts <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "candidate_verdicts.parquet"))
mit      <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "candidate_mitigation_summary.parquet"))

vc <- verdicts |> mutate(label = str_replace(candidate_label, " \\(.*\\)", ""))
n_new <- sum(vc$verdict == "new"); n_expand <- sum(vc$verdict == "expand")
n_adopt <- sum(vc$verdict == "adopt")
```

## What this is

Technical support for **categorical-exclusion (CE) development**: which recurring
clean-energy actions in prior Environmental Assessments that ended in a **Finding
of No Significant Impact (FONSI)** point to a CE opportunity? Per CEQ's April 2026
CE Guidance, prior EAs/FONSIs are explicit evidence for CE substantiation. The
model output is the BLM geothermal-exploration CE — a recognizable action with
explicit limits (≤10 acres, no new roads).

We start from the **452 clean-energy EA-source FONSI projects**, narrow to the
**CE-shaped subset** within each candidate action type, extract the bounding
limits and mitigation pattern, and cross-reference every candidate against the
**existing federal CE catalog** (CE Explorer, 2,105 CEs). Each candidate resolves
to one of three opportunity types:

- **New CE** — a recurring, bounded action that no existing CE covers.
- **Expand a CE** — an existing CE exists, but our FONSIs go beyond its stated limits.
- **Adopt a CE** — an existing CE exists at one agency that others doing the same work lack.

> **First-pass caveat.** This build is deterministic (the LLM-assisted extraction
> and verification pass is the next step). Treat the specific limits and the
> new/expand/adopt verdicts as **directional**, pending verification.

## The three opportunity lists

```{r verdict-table}
vc |>
  filter(verdict %in% c("new", "expand", "adopt")) |>
  arrange(factor(verdict, levels = c("new", "expand", "adopt")), desc(rank_score)) |>
  transmute(
    Candidate = label, Verdict = verdict,
    `CE-shaped FONSIs` = n_profile_fonsi,
    `Best existing CE` = best_ce_structured_id,
    `Adopt targets` = adopt_targets,
    `Rank` = round(rank_score, 2)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Candidate CE opportunities (new / expand / adopt)") |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Candidate categories by CE verdict (observed FONSI projects)."
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_verdicts.png"))
```

**Honest headline.** On the current candidate set, **`r n_new` are net-new** —
every strong clean-energy candidate already maps to an existing CE, so the
evidence supports **expanding and adopting** existing CEs (`r n_expand` expand,
`r n_adopt` adopt). Surfacing genuinely new CEs requires widening the search into
the action categories we set aside (a planned follow-up).

## Candidate evidence and mitigation

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-cap: ["CE-shaped evidence per candidate.", "Mitigated-FONSI share (Track B)."]
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_evidence_volume.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_mitigated_share.png"))
```

Mitigation is read two ways: a high *case-specific* mitigation share is a CE
**risk** (a CE can't lean on project-by-project mitigation), but a *consistent*
mitigation recurring across the class can become a **codifiable CE design
criterion** — and the agency's own boundary statements ("would be significant
absent X," "would require an EIS if it exceeded Y") hand us candidate limits.

## The existing-CE landscape

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Existing categorical exclusions per agency (top 15), from the CE Explorer catalog."
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_ce_per_agency.png"))
```

Of the 2,105 existing CEs, only ~90 state a numeric bound (e.g., transmission
reconductoring capped near 25 miles / 230 kV) — useful precedent for what a
defensible *expand* looks like. ~317 CEs are near-duplicates of a CE at another
agency, pointing to consolidation and cross-agency adoption opportunities.

## Wind — a contrast case

```{r}
wc <- vc |> filter(verdict == "contrast")
```

Wind (onshore) is kept as a **contrast**, not a recommendation: large footprints
and case-specific wildlife mitigation mean it genuinely needs case-by-case review,
and the existing wind CE (DOE B5.18) covers only very small installations. It
shows the method discriminates rather than green-lighting everything.

## Caveats & note to CATF

- Deterministic first pass: numeric limits and verdicts are directional until the
  LLM-assisted extraction/verification pass runs.
- Existing-CE matches are an embedding ranking aid, **not** verified coverage.
- "New" is empty here by construction — the current candidates are all already
  CE-covered; the net-new search (clustering set-aside action types) is the next step.

**For CATF:** this is a first pass. Tell us which opportunities to pursue — and
which specific CEs or technologies to investigate — and we fold them into the
next iteration.
